Figure_R1_adult_depth.description: Adult G2 comparison (MNE sample subject, 7,661 cortical targets, 10-nAm cortical-normal dipoles, 1-40 Hz, OPM 15 fT/sqrt(Hz)) against depth below the scalp (distance to the nearest MRI scalp point) in 5-mm bins; bins without a stored median are not drawn (65-70 mm: 3 targets). (a) The stored statistic is the median over the bin's targets of log2(d_OPM / d_Neuromag306) with its 25th and 75th percentiles (log2_ratio_vs_depth); it is drawn as 2**x, the median paired ratio of known-topography detectability with the oracle covariance. Line style = noise condition (sensor noise only; sensor + cortical brain noise, the primary condition, with its IQR shaded; brain noise + room field after the 8-term external projection), colour = OPM array. The grey numbers along the bottom of (a) are the targets per bin. (b) Signal only: per target the peak |B| of the OPM array over the peak |B| of the Neuromag magnetometers, median and IQR per bin (bridge_to_sphere.<array>_ratio_vs_depth), against the analytical sphere (radius 95 mm, Jas et al. Eq. 1, stored in bridge_to_sphere.sphere_ratio_vs_depth) at the bin centres with the real median standoffs (OPM matched sites and Neuromag magnetometers) and with the preprint's standoffs (0 / 18 mm). Both y axes are logarithmic with a line at a ratio of 1. No interval in this figure is a confidence interval: the shading is the spread over targets.
Figure_R1_adult_depth.alt: Two stacked line charts sharing a depth axis from 10 to 65 mm. Top: the OPM / Neuromag detectability ratio for the dense and matched OPM arrays under three noise conditions; with brain noise the dense array falls from 1.60 near the scalp to about 1.07 and the matched from 1.20 to about 0.94; with sensor noise only both are at or below 1; after the external projection both fall below 1 at depth. Bottom: the OPM / magnetometer peak-field ratio falls from about 5.4 to about 2.3 with depth, close to two analytical sphere curves.
Figure_R1_adult_depth.caption_draft: Figure R1. The OPM advantage is largest near the scalp. (a) Median paired detectability ratio OPM / Neuromag (306 channels) per 5-mm depth bin (7,658 of 7,661 targets in 11 bins; shaded: interquartile range over targets). With sensor and brain noise the dense array's ratio falls from 1.60 at 10-15 mm (n = 222) to 1.05-1.07 at 35-65 mm and the matched array's from 1.20 to 0.94-0.99. With sensor noise only the dense ratio is 1.00 at 10-15 mm and 0.64-0.86 deeper, the matched 0.47-0.71. After the external projection the dense ratio is below 1 from 45-50 mm (0.998) to 0.92 at 60-65 mm, the matched from 25-30 mm (0.985). (b) The signal alone: the median peak-field ratio OPM / Neuromag magnetometer falls from 5.41 (dense) and 4.90 (matched) at 10-15 mm to 2.28 and 2.25 at 55-60 mm (2.35 and 2.30 at 60-65 mm); the sphere with the real median standoffs (7.0 and 29.8 mm) gives 5.26 to 2.02 at the same bin centres, with the preprint's 0 / 18 mm 6.53 to 1.86. The OPM signal is larger at every depth; whether its detectability is higher depends on the noise (a).

Figure_R2_noise_model.description: The adult noise model in the 1-40 Hz band (G2, MNE sample recording). (a) In-band RMS per channel of each noise component, the square root of the median over channels of that component's variance (noise_composition, stored in T and T/m, drawn in fT and fT/cm): sensor (intrinsic) noise = ASD x sqrt(ENBW 35.1 Hz) with 15 fT/sqrt(Hz) for the OPM (declared, not a device value) and 3.5 fT/sqrt(Hz) and 3.6 fT/(cm sqrt(Hz)) for the Neuromag magnetometers and gradiometers (brochure values); brain = the distributed cortical background, its scale calibrated once on the Neuromag gradiometers; room field = the 8-term external field fitted to the Neuromag empty-room recording. The components are drawn side by side because RMS values do not add (variances do). (b) The only measured quantities, all from the Neuromag recording, against the model: the empty-room RMS (the model's room field is FITTED to this recording; it explains most of the magnetometers' empty-room variance but only the stated small share of the gradiometers', whose agreement is therefore a CHECK of the brochure sensor noise) and the brain noise (task baseline minus empty room): the gradiometer level is CALIBRATED, equal by construction, and the magnetometer level is the one independent PREDICTION (model / measured RMS 0.73). The x-axis labels give the per-channel spread of the model / measured brain-noise variance ratio (5th and 95th percentiles over channels; a variance ratio, not an RMS ratio). (c) The sensor-noise share of the in-band variance with brain noise and the room field, on the basis of (a): the sensor component's median channel variance over the sum of the three components' median channel variances, for the OPM arrays and for Neuromag's magnetometers and gradiometers separately. Nothing about the OPM noise is measured: its sensor noise is a declared white level and its brain and room noise are the Neuromag-calibrated model seen through the OPM arrays' own lead fields and coil responses.
Figure_R2_noise_model.alt: Three bar-chart panels. Top: modelled noise per channel by component; the OPM channels carry 494-525 fT of brain noise against 192 fT at the Neuromag magnetometers, similar room-field noise (about 113-116 fT) and 89 fT of sensor noise against 21 fT; gradiometers on their own fT/cm axis. Bottom left: measured versus model empty-room and brain noise for the Neuromag magnetometers and gradiometers, labelled fitted, check, predicted (0.73 times) and calibrated. Bottom right: sensor noise is 3.0 % of the dense OPM channels' variance, 0.9 % of the Neuromag magnetometers' and 24.8 % of its gradiometers'.
Figure_R2_noise_model.caption_draft: Figure R2. The noise model and what anchors it. (a) Modelled in-band (1-40 Hz) RMS noise per channel, sensor / brain / room field: OPM dense 89 / 494 / 114 fT, OPM matched 89 / 525 / 116 fT, Neuromag magnetometers 21 / 192 / 113 fT, gradiometers 21.3 / 37.1 / 1.7 fT/cm. (b) Measured vs model (Neuromag only): empty room 115.2 vs 114.9 fT (magnetometers) and 20.2 vs 21.4 fT/cm (gradiometers), with the room field fitted to this recording (explaining 94 % and 1.6 % of the variance, so the gradiometer agreement checks the brochure sensor noise); gradiometer brain noise 37.1 fT/cm, calibrated (equal by construction); magnetometer brain noise 262 fT measured vs 192 fT predicted (0.73x); per channel the model / measured brain-noise variance spans 0.13-0.78 (magnetometers) and 0.16-1.90 (gradiometers; 5th-95th percentiles). (c) Sensor noise is 3.0 % (dense) and 2.7 % (matched) of the OPM channels' in-band variance, 0.9 % of the Neuromag magnetometers' and 24.8 % of its gradiometers' (each component's median channel variance). No OPM noise was measured: the OPM sensor noise is declared, its brain and room noise are the Neuromag-calibrated model.

inputs: results/g2/g2_targets.csv :: region (the bootstrap groups: Desikan-Killiany parcels and medial-wall labels)
Figure_R3_conditions.description: Forest plot of the adult (G2) median over 7,661 cortical targets of the paired ratio OPM / Neuromag under every stored condition, for the dense and the matched OPM arrays and the triaxial control at the matched sites. Every value except the joint row is stored as median_log2 = the median over targets of log2(m_OPM / m_Neuromag) with a 95 % CI from a bootstrap over 70 parcels (the region labels of the targets: 68 Desikan-Killiany parcels and 2 medial-wall labels); it is drawn as 2**x. The joint OPM-noise x scalp-gap row (sensitivity_joint_asd_gap) is stored as a ratio with its CI from the same parcel bootstrap and is drawn as stored; the sensitivity rows used fewer bootstrap resamples than the primary rows (scripts/g2_adult_comparison.py). m is known-topography detectability with the oracle covariance except in the metric group: peak-channel SNR (the best single channel of each system; against the best of all 306 channels or of the 102 magnetometers), mean-power SNR (stored per target in dB; the analysis converted it to an amplitude ratio 10**(dB/20) before the same log2 summary, so it is on the amplitude scale of detectability), and plug-in detectability (Ledoit-Wolf covariance estimated from one common noise realization of 780 or 4,680 independent samples, the 2BT equivalent of 10 or 60 s in the 39-Hz-wide band, not estimates from coloured time series). Conditions vary one factor at a time from the primary (oracle covariance, sensor + brain noise, OPM 15 fT/sqrt(Hz), no scalp gap, 3-layer BEM, measured head position) except the joint row. The 1-layer BEM row is a convergence check on a random 1,000-target subset without an interval; on the same subset the 3-layer reference is 1.141 (dense) and 1.008 (matched). Grey row: the primary result; shaded vertical bands: each array's primary 95 % CI; logarithmic x axis with a line at 1; the right-hand columns repeat the medians (triangle: triaxial).
Figure_R3_conditions.alt: Forest plot with 21 rows in three groups (comparator, metric, noise and hardware). Each row shows the OPM / Neuromag median ratio with a 95 % interval for the dense array (dark blue circles) and the matched array (light blue squares) on a logarithmic axis with a line at 1. The dense array is below 1 in 3 of 19 rows (Peak-channel SNR vs the best of 306: 0.90; Sensor noise only: 0.74; 30 fT/sqrt(Hz) and a 3-mm gap (joint): 0.97); the matched array, 1.01 in the primary row, is below 1 in 8 of 19 rows. Two triaxial rows show a triaxial array at the matched sites.
Figure_R3_conditions.caption_draft: Figure R3. The adult ranking depends on the comparator, the metric and the OPM noise. Median ratio OPM / Neuromag over 7,661 targets with parcel-bootstrap 95 % CIs; values dense / matched. Primary (detectability against all 306 channels, sensor + brain noise): dense 1.144 [1.121-1.168], matched 1.009 [0.994-1.027]. Against the 204 gradiometers alone 1.33 / 1.13, the 102 magnetometers alone 1.19 / 1.04. Peak-channel SNR 0.90 / 0.85 against the best of the 306 channels and 1.23 / 1.14 against the best magnetometer; mean-power SNR 1.04 / 1.05; plug-in covariance 1.23 / 1.12 (780 samples) and 1.16 / 1.03 (4,680). Sensor noise only 0.74 / 0.53; with the room field 1.14 / 1.01; projected 1.12 / 0.95. OPM sensor noise 7, 10, 20, 30 fT/sqrt(Hz): 1.30, 1.23, 1.08, 1.01 (dense) and 1.08, 1.05, 0.98, 0.93 (matched; primary 15); scalp gap 3 mm 1.09 / 0.99, 6 mm 1.04 / 0.96; 30 fT/sqrt(Hz) with a 3-mm gap 0.968 [0.956-0.978] (dense) and 0.887 [0.861-0.904] (matched). Triaxial OPM at the matched sites 1.12 (1.05 with the tangential axes at twice the noise); 1-layer BEM 1.13 / 1.02 (1,000-target subset, no interval). One factor varied at a time except the joint row.

inputs: results/g2/g2_targets.csv :: region, lobe, depth_mm, amp_opm_dense, amp_squid_mag, detect_opm_dense_opm_intrinsic+brain, detect_opm_matched_opm_intrinsic+brain, detect_squid_combined_intrinsic+brain, detect_squid_mag_intrinsic+brain
Figure_R4_regions_adult.description: Adult (G2) comparison by brain region with sensor + brain noise, oracle covariance and OPM 15 fT/sqrt(Hz); both hemispheres pooled. Regions: the six Desikan-Killiany lobes of the study's grouping (the 558 medial-wall targets belong to no lobe) and three single parcels emphasised by the epilepsy literature: precentral, superior temporal ('lateral temporal') and parahippocampal (one of the two parcels of the report's mesial temporal group). (a, b) Bars start at a ratio of 1 on a logarithmic axis and end at the median over the region's targets of the paired detectability ratio OPM / Neuromag, against all 306 channels (a) or the 102 magnetometers (b). Lobes: median and 95 % parcel-bootstrap interval from g2_summary.json by_lobe (2**median_log2; a bootstrap over the lobe's own parcels: frontal 22, parietal 10, temporal 18, occipital 8, cingulate 8, insula 2 parcels, so an interval resting on few parcels is crude). Single parcels: the per-target ratio detect_<array>_opm_intrinsic+brain / detect_squid_<combined|mag>_intrinsic+brain from g2_targets.csv (values as stored, rounded), unweighted median and interquartile range over the parcel's targets (a spread, not a confidence interval; a parcel bootstrap is not possible within one parcel). (c) Median depth below the scalp (distance to the nearest scalp point) of the region's targets; (d) median over the region's targets of the peak-field ratio amp_opm_dense / amp_squid_mag (peak |B| of the dense OPM array over the best Neuromag magnetometer; signal only), both from g2_targets.csv. The n under each label is the number of targets; the lobe medians recomputed from the CSV agree with by_lobe.
Figure_R4_regions_adult.alt: Horizontal bar chart of nine brain regions: six lobes, then the precentral, superior temporal and parahippocampal parcels. For each region two bars give the OPM / Neuromag detectability ratio of the dense and matched arrays, against all 306 channels and against the 102 magnetometers; the dense array is above 1 in every region; against all channels the matched array is below 1 in temporal, cingulate, insula, parahippocampal. Two narrow panels give the median depth (23-49 mm) and the median peak-field ratio (2.4-3.8).
Figure_R4_regions_adult.caption_draft: Figure R4. The adult result by brain region (sensor + brain noise; both hemispheres). (a) Median detectability ratio OPM / Neuromag 306, dense / matched: frontal 1.22 / 1.04, parietal 1.14 / 1.04, temporal 1.16 / 0.99, occipital 1.12 / 1.02, cingulate 1.05 / 0.99, insula 1.09 / 0.95 (lobes, 95 % parcel-bootstrap intervals); precentral 1.21 / 1.06, superior temporal ('lateral temporal') 1.16 / 1.01, parahippocampal 1.12 / 0.92 (single parcels, interquartile ranges over targets). (b) Against the 102 magnetometers alone: frontal 1.28 / 1.08, parietal 1.18 / 1.08, temporal 1.21 / 1.02, occipital 1.15 / 1.05, cingulate 1.06 / 1.00, insula 1.11 / 0.98, precentral 1.26 / 1.10, superior temporal 1.21 / 1.05, parahippocampal 1.18 / 0.96. (c, d) Median depth below the scalp and median peak-field ratio OPM dense / magnetometer: frontal 23.6 mm / 3.85, parietal 25.9 mm / 3.25, temporal 26.7 mm / 3.02, occipital 31.3 mm / 3.01, cingulate 48.6 mm / 2.57, insula 42.6 mm / 2.70, precentral 23.0 mm / 3.77, superior temporal 28.3 mm / 3.11, parahippocampal 28.7 mm / 2.43. Targets: frontal 2,532, parietal 2,016, temporal 1,240, occipital 499, cingulate 558, insula 258, precentral 526, superior temporal 281, parahippocampal 92.
